summary: Today's best opening is a Lane C story. Retatrutide's two Phase 3 sleep apnea trials (TRIUMPH-1-OSA, n=243, no diabetes; TRIUMPH-2-OSA, n=448, type 2 diabetes) were published in NEJM and picked up by MedPage (Oct 21), HCPLive, Physicians Weekly and Medical Dialogues (Oct 23). Few creators have covered it, and retatrutide-named Shorts are our best Short category (median 120). Make the same-day long-form with "Retatrutide" first in the title, then a 20:00 funnel Short. Second is Lane B: CBS News (Oct 21) bought and lab-tested vials sold as "retatrutide". The corner-store vial held phenylacetic acid instead of the drug, plus 13 bacterial colonies. Lilly referenced 2 deaths CBS had previously reported. All of this can be credited and dated, and it builds on our proven "what's confirmed" format. Never name a seller. Rising third is GLP-1 and alcohol: the Lancet semaglutide alcohol use disorder RCT, Heineken's beer-sales warning (Reuters and Guardian, Oct 23) and STAT on off-label telehealth prescribing (Oct 22). It needs an honest-uncertainty frame. Strong Lane A search pieces: Wegovy pill vs shot (pegged to new JAMA Network Open uptake data, Oct 22), tirzepatide side effects, stopping GLP-1s, and GLP-1s before surgery. Honest-uncertainty Shorts are being tested after the macular Short hit 105 on YouTube and 160 on Instagram: GLP-1s while breastfeeding (WSJ, Oct 23), genes and GLP-1 response, and menopause hormone therapy with semaglutide. Skip carousels. The compounded recall is peaking and we already used this week's one recall Short. Reject the sourcing and reconstitution guides for research peptides and the compounded-to-tirzepatide switching how-tos.

candidates.topic: Retatrutide for sleep apnea: two Phase 3 trials in NEJM. TRIUMPH-1-OSA (243 adults with obesity or overweight, no diabetes) and TRIUMPH-2-OSA (448 with type 2 diabetes), 80 weeks
candidates.angle: Lane C, 'New GLP-1 Drug Decoded'. Same-day long-form titled 'Retatrutide for Sleep Apnea: What the New Trials Show'. Without diabetes, apnea events fell by 34.3 an hour (9 mg) and 31.7 an hour (12 mg), versus 9.9 on placebo. With type 2 diabetes the falls were 24.7 and 25.4, versus 10.3. Say the trial dose names once each and make clear they are trial doses, not dosing advice. Gastrointestinal side effects were the most common. Status: investigational, not approved. Compare with tirzepatide, already approved for moderate-to-severe obstructive sleep apnea with obesity (SURMOUNT-OSA, a separate trial, so it's an indirect comparison). The 20:00 funnel Short is 'Retatrutide and Sleep Apnea: How Much Did Breathing Pauses Drop?'. Talk to your doctor or prescriber about whether it's right for you.
candidates.why_now: The full NEJM publication of two parallel randomized trials was covered by MedPage Today (Oct 21) and by HCPLive, Physicians Weekly and Medical Dialogues (Oct 22–23). It is a named next-gen drug with a new peer-reviewed result, which is exactly our Lane C criterion (median 44, EloraTZP 489). Retatrutide Shorts have a median of 120.

evidence.signal: TRIUMPH-1-OSA n=243 and TRIUMPH-2-OSA n=448; AHI changes by arm vs placebo at 80 weeks; GI events most common
'Lilly's retatrutide creeps closer to market for sleep apnea'
TRIUMPH-1 OSA basket topline: AHI down up to 36.1 events an hour (60.6%), released earlier in 2026
Press release: 'Obesity drug may also help treat obstructive sleep apnoea'

candidates.topic: Retatrutide online: what CBS News found when it lab-tested vials sold as 'retatrutide' (Oct 21, 2026). The corner-store vial held phenylacetic acid and 13 bacterial colonies; Lilly referenced 2 deaths CBS had previously reported
candidates.angle: Lane B, 'What's Actually Confirmed?'. Long-form titled 'Retatrutide Online: What a Lab Test Found (Oct 2026)'. Credit every line, with the date, to CBS News (Oct 21, 2026), the University of Iowa testing, Lilly's statement or the FDA. Two online samples looked like basic retatrutide but were not identical to Lilly's trial version. Never name the seller or the store, never explain buying, and never imply any source is 'safe'. Close by pointing viewers to a prescriber about approved options or clinical trials. Short: 'Retatrutide Vials Tested: What the Lab Found'. Pinned comment asks people to share, not to say where they buy. No emoji.
candidates.why_now: The CBS national investigation (Oct 21) and the Penn AI Reddit study (ScienceDaily, Oct 21–22) are in mainstream press. 'FDA concerns about unapproved GLP-1 drugs: retatrutide' search pages are multiplying. Lilly and the FDA are arguing over jurisdiction (Capitol Forum, Oct 21). Gray-market 'what's confirmed' Shorts have a median of 106.

evidence.signal: Lab results: phenylacetic acid and 13 bacterial colonies in a corner-store vial; Lilly statement; Yale physician quoted
'People are taking an unapproved weight-loss drug. AI found something surprising' (Penn Reddit study)

candidates.topic: Semaglutide and alcohol: a Lancet RCT found fewer heavy drinking days in alcohol use disorder with obesity (108 adults, 26 weeks, plus CBT), and Heineken now warns that GLP-1s could cut beer sales (Oct 23)
candidates.angle: Honest-uncertainty frame: 'Do GLP-1s Make You Drink Less? What the Trial Can and Can't Say'. Heavy drinking days fell about 13.7 percentage points more than placebo, and liver markers improved. Always name the population (alcohol use disorder with obesity). Semaglutide is not approved for alcohol use disorder, and STAT reports telehealth firms are prescribing it off-label. Don't encourage that. Say 'talk to your doctor'. Explain the brain reward pathway (pillar: how GLP-1 works). Heineken works as a news hook only.
candidates.why_now: Reuters' exclusive, the Guardian and BeverageDaily all covered the Heineken document on Oct 23. STAT (Oct 22) reported off-label addiction prescribing by telehealth. BMJ (Oct 20) covered a planned US trial testing whether semaglutide reduces crime. Several independent source types are converging.

evidence.signal: Lancet RCT: semaglutide 2.4 vs placebo, 54 per arm, 26 weeks, heavy drinking days down 13.7 points more
Heineken document reveals worries over weight-loss drugs and beer sales (Oct 23)
Telehealth prescribing GLP-1s off-label for addiction ahead of any FDA approval (Oct 22)

candidates.topic: Wegovy pill vs Wegovy shot: what's the difference? New JAMA Network Open data (Oct 22): about 149,000 US adults started the pill in its first 12 weeks, 36% of them new to GLP-1 medicines
candidates.angle: Lane A, 'Head-to-Head'. Title: 'Wegovy Pill vs Wegovy Shot: What's the Difference?'. Cover how each is taken (daily pill vs weekly shot, without dosing detail), what their trials showed, common side effects for each, and who might ask their doctor about which. New fact: pill uptake briefly rivalled the injection in the first weeks after approval. Talk to your doctor or prescriber about whether it's right for you. Don't switch on your own.
candidates.why_now: HealthDay, Medical Xpress and AJMC covered the JAMA Network Open study on Oct 22–23. Search-question pages like 'wegovy pill pros and cons', 'how effective is wegovy pill' and 'when is the wegovy pill coming out' are spawning. The pill is also launching in France (Oct 21).

evidence.signal: 148,792 initiators Dec 22, 2025–Mar 15, 2026; 36.1% new to GLP-1; peaked near the injectable level
'Oral semaglutide caught on quickly after obesity approval'

candidates.topic: Tirzepatide (Mounjaro) side effects: which are common and what helps. The Conversation (Oct 22) says nausea needs closer study, and a new Neurogastroenterol Motil review covers GI symptoms and motility
candidates.angle: Lane A, 'Life on GLP-1'. Title: 'Tirzepatide Side Effects: Which Are Common and What Helps'. Explain why slower gastric emptying causes nausea, which effects tend to ease over time, and practical habits (smaller meals, stopping at fullness, hydration, less fat). Say when to call your prescriber. No dose changes. Chapters named after searched questions. Funnel Short the next day.
keywords: how long does mounjaro nausea last
candidates.why_now: Seen in 5 snapshots. The Conversation (Oct 22) and a fresh motility review give a news hook, and Drugwatch's side-effects page is ranking. It is a core Lane A query, and side-effect Reels do well on Instagram (103).

evidence.signal: Review of GI symptom events and motility changes with GLP-1 RAs
'GLP-1 drugs change how people eat, but nausea needs closer study' (Oct 22)

candidates.topic: Retatrutide and the kidneys: lower albumin in the urine and lower kidney filtration pressure in obesity and chronic kidney disease (HCPLive, Oct 22)
candidates.angle: Lane C companion or a retatrutide Short: 'Retatrutide and Kidneys: What the New Data Show'. Higher doses lowered albuminuria in Phase 2 analyses, and some kidney measures improved in people without diabetes but not in those with type 2 diabetes. Say plainly that this is mid-stage evidence. The TRANSCEND-CKD and TRIUMPH-Outcomes trials are still running. Compare with semaglutide's FLOW trial (type 2 diabetes with CKD) as the approved benchmark.
candidates.why_now: HCPLive (Oct 22), Newsweek (Oct 23) on GLP-1s and kidney health, and Psychiatrist.com on kidney protection, plus a Kidney International FLOW safety paper (Oct 20). Kidney is a recurring body-effect theme.

evidence.signal: 'Retatrutide Lowers Albuminuria, Glomerular Pressure in Obesity and CKD' (Oct 22)
Safety outcomes of semaglutide by CKD severity in FLOW (Oct 20)
Design and baseline of the retatrutide CKD trial

candidates.topic: Can GLP-1 medicines be used while breastfeeding? WSJ (Oct 23) plus JAMA (Oct 1): GLP-1 starts among new mothers rose about 24-fold, from under 0.1% in 2018 to nearly 2% in early 2025
candidates.angle: Honest uncertainty: 'Semaglutide While Breastfeeding: What the Evidence Can't Say Yet'. Name the worry and say it's understandable. Small studies on transfer into milk exist (one PubMed infant-safety study), and a dedicated lactation trial is registered. The JAMA data couldn't tell who was breastfeeding. Also cover why these medicines are avoided in pregnancy. Decide with your prescriber and pediatrician. No advice to start or stop.
candidates.why_now: The WSJ feature (Oct 23) follows the JAMA study, an ABC News segment and a podcaster's announcement. Searches are very personal for women of reproductive age. Tests the honest-uncertainty format that scored 160 on Instagram.

evidence.signal: JAMA Oct 1: postpartum GLP-1 use rose about 24-fold; breastfeeding status unknown
Subcutaneous semaglutide during breastfeeding: infant safety and transfer into milk (small study)
Effects of GLP-1 RAs on human lactation outcomes (registered study)

candidates.topic: Can your genes predict how well tirzepatide or semaglutide works? MindBodyGreen and Yahoo (Oct 23) revisit the Nature 23andMe study of 27,885 users: a GLP1R variant was linked to more weight loss, and a GIPR variant to nausea on tirzepatide only
candidates.angle: Honest-uncertainty Short: 'Tirzepatide and Your Genes: What This Study Can't Say'. Each GLP1R variant copy was linked to about 0.76 kg more weight loss, which is small. The GIPR variant was linked to nausea on tirzepatide but not semaglutide. The study is observational and self-reported, and no gene test is recommended to choose a drug. Don't promote consumer DNA tests.
keywords: why ozempic doesn't work for me
candidates.why_now: Fresh consumer coverage on Oct 23 (MindBodyGreen, then Yahoo syndication) and a registered genetic-prediction trial. It ties into our live Lane A video 'How Long Does Tirzepatide Take to Work?', which works as a funnel.

evidence.signal: Summary of why weight-loss drug response varies
Genetic prediction of response to GLP-1/GIP agonists (prospective)
'Your Genes May Predict How Your Body Reacts To GLP-1s' (Oct 23)

candidates.topic: Menopause hormone therapy and GLP-1 weight loss: about 3,900 women aged 45+ (about 2,400 on semaglutide, about 1,500 on tirzepatide), observational, Menopause Society 2026
candidates.angle: Short: 'Semaglutide After Menopause: Does Hormone Therapy Change Results?'. Semaglutide with hormone therapy was linked to about 11% weight loss at 1 year, versus 9.5% without. Keep the 2026 tirzepatide finding separate from the 2025 Mayo tirzepatide study (19.2% vs 14%) and check which figures belong to which study. Say 'linked to', and say hormone therapy shouldn't be started for weight loss.
candidates.why_now: Patient Care Online (Oct 23) and Powers Health (Oct 21). It pairs with the CagriSema menopause-stage analysis from the last snapshot, and women 45–65 are a core high-ad-value audience.

evidence.signal: About 3,900 women; semaglutide plus hormone therapy about 11% vs 9.5% at 1 year

evidence.source: Patient Care Online via Google News

candidates.topic: What happens when you stop semaglutide or tirzepatide? SURMOUNT-4 and STEP 1 extension regain data, plus real-world early discontinuation (Diabetes Obes Metab, Oct 19)
candidates.angle: Lane A, 'Life on GLP-1'. Title: 'What Happens When You Stop Semaglutide or Tirzepatide?'. Use the regain curves, explain why appetite returns, and cover what the evidence says helps keep results (strength training, protein, habits). Explicitly no stopping or tapering advice: plan any change with your prescriber.
